explanation: Surfactants solubilize oils into micelles, enabling removal with minimal rinse water.
Enzymes/microbes digest organic soils into soluble fragments for easier low-water extraction.
Generate reactive oxidants in situ (plasma/electrochemical) to decompose stains without bulk water.
Use vaporization/condensation and pressure swings to dissolve and recover contaminants with minimal liquid.
Supercritical/near‑critical fluids act as non-liquid solvents to dissolve and extract contaminants without water.

labels.name: Localized controlled dosing and triggered release

explanation: Deliver micro-droplets or thin solvent films to stain sites, minimizing overall wetting and water use.
Sealed high-humidity/minimal-liquid chamber uses vapor-phase cleaning to treat garments without bulk water.
Filter and separate contaminants from transport fluid, recirculating cleaned water/solvent for reuse.
Engineered sorbents adsorb soils, then are regenerated to release contaminants and reuse sorbent and fluid.

labels.name: Localized controlled dosing and triggered release

explanation: Microcapsules release concentrated cleaning actives on trigger, localizing chemistry and reducing water needs.

labels.name: Stimulus-responsive surface release and removable coatings

explanation: Apply peelable film that binds soils and is removed mechanically to extract contaminants without heavy rinsing.

labels.name: Foam- and bubble-mediated flotation and lift

explanation: Foams or bubbles attach to hydrophobic soils and lift them away for collection, minimizing textile wetting.
Solid pads or particles abrade or transfer soils from fibers for subsequent low-water removal.
Tumbling and collisions mechanically dislodge soils and reorient fabrics for easier extraction.
Ultrasound, acoustic waves or air pulses break soil–fiber bonds and eject contaminants without large water volumes.
Electric/ionic/magnetic fields move or concentrate charged/magnetic particles for capture without bulk solvent transport.
Electrowetting controls local wetting to mobilize droplets and remove soils only where needed.
Vacuum/suction lifts and entrains loosened particles and gases away from textiles with minimal liquid.
Force fluid through fabric pores to flush entrained contaminants out using targeted flow.
Maintain a gentle extraction flow to continuously capture suspended particles without disrupting fabrics.
Uses freeze/thaw phase-change cycles to create stresses that pry out embedded dirt.
Targeted IR/microwave/RF heating selectively warms soils to loosen adhesion while sparing fabric.
Generate shockwaves/pressure impulses to fracture soil–fiber bonds and eject contaminants for capture.
Chelators and adsorbents sequester metal-bound or hydrophobic soils into removable complexes.

labels.name: Stimulus-responsive surface release and removable coatings

explanation: Change surface adhesion via stimuli-responsive coatings or triggers to release and capture contaminants.
Apply electrical currents to destabilize colloids and aggregate fine contaminants for easier filtration.
Modify fluid rheology with fields/additives so stresses preferentially release adhered particles.
Detect stains and apply localized sprays/heating/mechanics to treat only contaminated areas, minimizing water.
